summary: Iteration-8 fully validated the WhatsApp-style multi-room Chat rewrite (Family + Groups + Direct). Authored /app/backend/tests/test_chat_rooms.py — 26 tests across 9 classes: (1) GET /api/chat/rooms — Family room always present with id==tree_id, pinned first, correct member_count/shape (last_message, last_message_at, unread, member_count, name); solo user sees only family. (2) GET /api/chat/contacts — excludes self, returns {user_id,name,picture,role} for every OTHER member. (3) POST /api/chat/group — admin creates (creator auto-added, bogus member_ids filtered), editor also allowed, viewer -> 403, empty name -> 400. (4) POST /api/chat/direct — idempotent via dm_key (A->B and B->A return same room id), 400 for self, 404 for a user not in the tree (X in T2 was rejected by T1). (5) GET /api/chat?room_id — family default works, viewer sees can_send=false on family, direct room_name = OTHER participant's name, 403 for non-member of group AND non-participant of direct. (6) POST /api/chat — admin can send family, viewer cannot (403), group participant OK, non-participant 403, reply_to snapshot preserved (id echoed), empty message 400. (7) Deceased rule — user D whose linked people doc has is_alive=false AND death_date got 403 with detail 'Anggota yang telah meninggal tidak dapat mengirim pesan' in BOTH family and direct room (get-or-create direct still worked, only POST /chat is blocked); unlinked viewer C could still send in a group. (8) Backward compatibility — legacy family_chat doc with room_id==tree_id is returned by GET /api/chat (no room_id) AND by GET /api/chat?room_id=<tree_id>. (9) Unread counts — after A sends 2 msgs to a fresh A<->E DM, E's GET /api/chat/rooms shows unread=2 with last_message preview; after E opens GET /api/chat?room_id=<dm>, unread resets to 0. Result: 26/26 PASSED (100%). Post-run cleanup verified: 0 leftover TEST_CHAT_* users/people/trees/chat_rooms/family_chat; real users (Erick De vries, MST) and their trees/people untouched — never used delete_many({}). No bugs found in the chat multi-room implementation. Deprecated packages detected: none observed in scope (backend-only test).
action_items: No functional bugs found in Chat rooms/groups/direct/deceased-rule. Ready for frontend wiring.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:833 resolve_room queries chat_rooms by {id,tree_id}. Combined with the room_id==tid short-circuit on L830, this correctly makes the Family room a virtual sibling — no dependency on a chat_rooms row for the tree. Good.
server.py:836 non-participant of a custom room returns 403. Correct per spec.

server.py:809 is_user_deceased matches people doc by user's email in the given tree. Note: user email is used as the join key — if a person is renamed but email changes on the user side (from Google), the link may drift. Not in test scope; flagging for later.
server.py:816-818 alive resolution: is_alive when present, else derived from death_date. Confirmed both paths (D has is_alive=False AND death_date; either alone would also trigger the block).
server.py:832 can_send for family = my_role in (admin,editor). Viewer explicitly false. Matches spec.

server.py:948 list_chat_rooms — Family room is synthesized from tree_members on every call (not stored). Ensures the Family room is always available even for trees created before the multi-room feature. Good migration story.
server.py:961 unread count excludes sender_id==uid — so self-sent messages don't inflate. Correct.
server.py:1029 create_group returns _serialize([{...}])[0] with the full doc including created_by/created_at. Consider adding an explicit response_model to lock the shape.
server.py:1041-1043 dm_key = f\"{tree_id}:{a}:{b}\" with sorted pair guarantees idempotency across A->B and B->A. Verified.

server.py:1039 open_direct membership check uses find_one on tree_members but does NOT check for {deleted_at: None} — none of the schema uses soft-delete on tree_members so this is safe today, flagging for consistency.

server.py:1120-1127 send_chat order: role check first, then deceased check. Means a viewer in a group who is deceased will hit the 403-'meninggal' (since can_send is True on group). Verified with C (viewer) NOT deceased sending in group succeeds; D (editor, deceased) blocked in family AND direct. Behavior matches rule (2) + rule (3).

server.py:1113 delete_chat calls resolve_tree with m.get('room_id') — for legacy messages room_id == tree_id so this still resolves. For NEW messages (group/direct), room_id is a chat_rooms.id which is NOT a tree_id — resolve_tree({tree_id: <room_id>}) will 403 for a non-member of a nonexistent tree with that id. BUG POTENTIAL: DELETE /api/chat/{msg_id} may 403/404 on messages sent to groups/direct rooms because resolve_tree is called with the room_id, not the tree_id. Recommend passing m.get('tree_id') instead. Not covered by current tests (delete is out-of-scope for the review request) but flagging for main agent.
seed_data_creation: test_chat_rooms.py seeds 6 synthetic users (A admin, B editor, C viewer, D editor-deceased-linked, E viewer, X outsider) + sessions directly in Mongo, plus 2 synthetic trees (T1 with 5 members, T2 with 2). Inserts 4 people docs in T1 linking A/B/E as alive and D as DECEASED (is_alive=False, death_date='2020-05-10'); C is intentionally unlinked. All ids tracked in module-scope CREATED registry; teardown deletes ONLY those tracked docs plus chat_rooms/family_chat/app_notifications/chat_typing scoped to our tree_ids. Never delete_many({}). Post-run scan: 0 leftover TEST_CHAT_* docs.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Re-run: `cd /app/backend/tests && pytest test_chat_rooms.py -n 0 -v` (requires -n 0: module-scope CREATED registry and MongoDB session). Uses BASE_URL from EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL and Bearer session tokens seeded directly in user_sessions. NEVER runs delete_many({}) — only removes tracked ids. Endpoints verified: GET /api/chat/rooms, GET /api/chat/contacts, POST /api/chat/group, POST /api/chat/direct, GET /api/chat (?room_id or default), POST /api/chat (family/group/direct + deceased + reply_to + mentions), backward-compat legacy row insertion. Family room id is asserted equal to tree_id. Deceased detail string checked for the word 'meninggal' (case-insensitive) so string tweaks won't false-fail. NOT covered (out of scope): DELETE /api/chat/{msg_id} for group/direct messages — see critical_code_review_comments last entry for a latent bug.
